open_points.subject: staff-session transport
open_points.text: “managed sessions with expiry, revocation, and sign-out-everywhere” does not say how a successful staff login returns the session or how later staff requests carry it; R0-09 specifies this only for viewers and producers
open_points.question: How is a StaffSession delivered and authenticated on subsequent HTTP requests: a protected browser cookie, a bearer token, or another named mechanism?
options: Host-only HTTP-only secure cookie
Bearer token returned in JSON
Separate explicitly named staff transport
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only HTTP-only secure same-site cookie, parallel to ViewerSession but with its own cookie and policy.

witness.initial: An active verified staff account has no session.
events: The staff member submits valid login credentials.
The client makes an authenticated project request.
outcomes: Login sets a protected cookie, and the project request authenticates from that cookie.
Login returns a token in JSON, and the project request must send an Authorization header.
witness.observer: The staff client and every HTTP/API implementer

open_points.subject: staff session revocation and sign-out-everywhere
open_points.text: “managed sessions with expiry, revocation, and sign-out-everywhere”
open_points.question: Who may revoke one staff session or invoke sign-out-everywhere, what identifies the target sessions, and what observable result or concealed failure does each action produce?
options: The holder can end one or all of their own sessions; administrators can also revoke them
Only the holder can sign out; account suspension/disable is the only administrative revocation
Administrators manage individual sessions through access management
open_points.default_guess: Allow the holder to end the current session or all of their sessions, and administrators to revoke all sessions by suspending or disabling the account.

witness.initial: A staff account has two valid sessions on different devices.
events: The holder invokes sign-out-everywhere from the first session.
The second device makes another authenticated request.
outcomes: Both sessions are invalidated, including the session that invoked the action.
Only the other sessions are invalidated, leaving the invoking session usable.
witness.observer: The staff member using the two devices

open_points.subject: viewer access-link reissue and established sessions
open_points.text: The credential is “re-issuable,” revoking it “closes all of that client's projects,” and Q13 says issuing a code already revokes earlier ones, but the text does not state whether sessions established with an earlier credential are invalidated by reissue
open_points.question: When a new ViewerAccessCredential is issued and earlier credentials are revoked, do ViewerSessions created through those earlier credentials stop working immediately?
options: Invalidate every session established from a revoked credential
Keep established sessions until expiry or explicit session revocation
Invalidate all sessions of the viewer whenever any access credential is reissued
open_points.default_guess: Invalidate every session derived from the superseded credential immediately.

witness.initial: A viewer entered through credential A and has an active ViewerSession.
events: An administrator reissues the access link, creating credential B and revoking A.
The viewer uses the existing session created from A to read a project.
outcomes: The request is rejected because reissue closed sessions derived from A.
The request succeeds because A was needed only to create the still-valid session.
witness.observer: The viewer and the administrator performing the reissue

open_points.subject: service-credential rotation overlap
open_points.text: Credentials are “rotatable with an overlap period”
open_points.question: What starts and ends the overlap period, how long is it, and what happens to the old credential when it ends?
options: A fixed configured duration followed by automatic revocation
Administrator supplies an expiry when rotating
Both credentials remain valid until an administrator explicitly revokes the old one
open_points.default_guess: Use a configured fixed overlap duration and automatically revoke the superseded credential at its end.

witness.initial: A service principal authenticates with credential A.
events: An administrator rotates the credential and receives credential B.
After some elapsed time, the producer sends one import with A and another with B.
outcomes: A has automatically expired while B succeeds.
Both A and B continue to succeed until an explicit revocation.

open_points.subject: staff account status lifecycle
open_points.text: The text names `pending_verification`, `active`, suspension, disabling, activation and reinstatement, but does not define the allowed transitions or distinguish suspension from disabling
open_points.question: What are the complete StaffAccount statuses and allowed administrator actions between them, and what lasting differences exist between suspended and disabled accounts?
options: Suspended is reversible and disabled is terminal
Both are reversible but retain distinct administrative meanings
Use one inactive status despite both words appearing
open_points.default_guess: Treat both as reversible inactive states, with explicit transitions back to active and immediate session invalidation on entry.

witness.initial: An active staff account has a valid session and an assignment.
events: An administrator disables the account.
Later the administrator attempts to reinstate it.
outcomes: Reinstatement is a supported transition and the assignment again permits new sessions and access.
Disabled is terminal, so the account cannot be reinstated and a replacement account is required.
witness.observer: The administrator and the affected staff member

open_points.subject: holder password change
open_points.text: “the holder logs in with the initial password and changes it” and the named contract `change_staff_password` do not say what authorizes the change, whether the current password is required, or what happens to existing sessions
open_points.question: What input and authorization does a staff holder's password-change action require, and which existing StaffSessions remain valid after success?
options: Authenticated session plus current password; revoke all other sessions
Authenticated session alone; retain all sessions
Authenticated session plus current password; revoke every session including the current one
open_points.default_guess: Require an authenticated session and current password, keep the invoking session, and revoke all other sessions.

witness.initial: A staff account has two valid sessions and its initial password.
events: The holder changes the password from session A.
Session B makes another request.
outcomes: Session B is rejected because password change revoked other sessions.
Session B remains valid because sessions are independent of the password after creation.

open_points.subject: first-administrator audit
open_points.text: R0-07 says the bootstrap command is “never printed, logged or audited,” while Audit and invariant 12 say “Every significant action carries actor provenance to audit”
open_points.question: Is creation of the first administrator an explicit exception to the universal audit invariant, or must the bootstrap create an audit record without recording its secret inputs?
options: Explicitly exempt bootstrap from product audit
Audit bootstrap success/failure and administrator identity while excluding password material
open_points.default_guess: Audit the bootstrap outcome and created administrator identity, never the password.

witness.initial: The deployment contains no staff account.
events: The host operator successfully runs the local bootstrap command.
An auditor inspects portal audit records.
outcomes: No record exists because R0-07 forbids auditing the command.
A bootstrap/account-creation record exists because every significant action must be audited.

open_points.subject: sessionless bootstrap exception
open_points.text: Invariant 2 says “The operations without a session are those of R0-15,” but R0-07 defines a sessionless local command that creates the first administrator and R0-15 does not list it
open_points.question: Does the exhaustive sessionless-operation statement exclude non-HTTP host commands, or must R0-07 bootstrap be added as an explicit exception?
options: Limit invariant 2 and R0-15 to HTTP operations
Add the local bootstrap command to the exhaustive exception list
Require a separate host authentication/session concept for bootstrap
open_points.default_guess: State that the exhaustive list applies to HTTP operations and explicitly acknowledge R0-07 as a non-HTTP exception.

witness.initial: An empty deployment has no principal or session.
events: The host operator invokes the R0-07 command.
outcomes: The command succeeds as the sessionless bootstrap specified by R0-07.
The command is forbidden by the invariant's exhaustive session requirement because it is absent from R0-15.
witness.observer: The host operator and bootstrap implementer

open_points.subject: bootstrap secret input channel
open_points.text: R0-07 says email and password are read “neither from process arguments nor from the environment nor from a file” but does not name the channel from which they are read
open_points.question: Through what concrete channel does the local command obtain the email and password, and what happens when that channel is unavailable or ends prematurely?
options: Interactive terminal prompts with hidden password entry
Standard input using a defined framing protocol
Operating-system credential facility
open_points.default_guess: Read both through interactive terminal prompts, suppress password echo, and fail with a defined code when no TTY is available.

witness.initial: An empty deployment is being provisioned by a non-interactive deployment script.
events: The script starts the bootstrap command without arguments, environment secrets, or a file.
outcomes: The command reads a defined standard-input payload and can complete non-interactively.
The command requires an interactive TTY and fails.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment script

open_points.subject: bootstrap exit-code contract
open_points.text: “Its outcome is a closed set of exit codes that deployment scripts may branch on”
open_points.question: What is the complete exit-code set and which condition—success, staff already exists, invalid input, configuration/storage failure, or interrupted secret input—maps to each code?
options: Distinct stable code for every branchable condition
Success, already-initialized, and one generic failure code
Only conventional success/failure codes
open_points.default_guess: Define stable distinct codes for success, already initialized, invalid input, and operational failure.

witness.initial: A deployment already contains one staff account.
events: A deployment script invokes bootstrap again.
The script branches on the process exit code.
outcomes: It receives a dedicated already-initialized code and treats the deployment as complete.
It receives a generic failure code indistinguishable from a database or configuration failure.
witness.observer: The deployment script and host operator

open_points.subject: readiness contract
open_points.text: R0-11 says the service “answers an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check” but does not define what readiness tests, or the status/body returned for ready, not-ready, live, and not-live states
open_points.question: Which conditions make the service ready versus merely live, and what stable HTTP status and body does each check return in every state?
options: Readiness requires validated configuration plus usable SQLite and binary root; liveness only requires the process event loop
Readiness requires only completed startup; liveness and readiness otherwise have identical semantics
Readiness additionally checks external Registry availability
open_points.default_guess: Make liveness process-local; make readiness require completed startup, usable SQLite, and usable configured binary root, but not Registry availability, with fixed non-diagnostic responses.

witness.initial: The process is running, but its SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: An orchestrator calls liveness.
The orchestrator calls readiness.
outcomes: Liveness succeeds and readiness fails.
Both checks succeed because startup completed and dependencies are not probed.

open_points.subject: uniform binary-read failure
open_points.text: “An unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize or unlisted read is answered the same way” does not say what that common answer is
open_points.question: What exact observable HTTP failure—status, media type, body, and relevant headers—is shared by all protected-binary denial and nonexistence cases?
options: 404 with a fixed empty body
404 with a fixed JSON error
403 with a fixed concealed response
open_points.default_guess: Return the same 404 response with a fixed non-diagnostic body and no object-derived headers.

witness.initial: A caller has a valid session and access to project A but not project B.
events: The caller requests an unknown document id.
The caller requests a known document belonging to project B.
outcomes: Both requests return a fixed empty 404 response.
Both requests return a fixed concealed JSON error or another uniformly chosen status.
witness.observer: The authenticated caller and HTTP client implementer

open_points.subject: OCR expense replay
open_points.text: Expense intake says “replay is idempotent,” while invariant 6 states only that one `recognized_document_id` creates at most one Expense; no text says what a replay returns or what happens when the repeated identity carries different project, content, total, document reference, or allocation
open_points.question: What observable result is returned for an identical expense replay, and which differing fields turn a repeated `recognized_document_id` into a conflict rather than an update or an idempotent replay?
options: Return the existing Expense for an identical replay and reject any differing business content as an integrity conflict
Return a fresh intake-result record naming the existing Expense, mirroring snapshot imports
Treat every repeated identity as success naming the original Expense regardless of differing submitted content
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing Expense for byte-equivalent normalized business content and reject any material difference as an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: `recognized_document_id` R already created Expense E in project A for EUR 100.
events: An operator submits R again for project A with total EUR 120.
The operator observes the response and then reads E.
outcomes: The replay is rejected as an integrity conflict and E remains EUR 100.
The request is treated as idempotent and returns E without disclosing that the submitted total differed.

open_points.subject: idempotent snapshot-republication HTTP outcome
open_points.text: An identical republication “is answered with a fresh import result of outcome idempotent replay that names the existing snapshot” but the success/failure classification of that answer is not stated
open_points.question: Is an idempotent replay an HTTP success, a conflict, or another stable response category, and is the fresh import result returned synchronously in the response body?
options: Successful response carrying the fresh import result
Conflict response carrying the fresh import result
Accepted/asynchronous response requiring a later R0-21 read
open_points.default_guess: Return a synchronous successful response whose JSON body is the fresh immutable import result.

witness.initial: Snapshot S for an estimate identity has already been accepted.
events: The producer republishes identical content.
The producer's client branches on the HTTP status before reading the body.
outcomes: The client follows its success path and stores the new `import_id`.
The client follows its conflict/error path even though the replay is idempotent.

open_points.subject: classified snapshot-import rejections
open_points.text: R0-25 records “every import attempt it classifies — accepted, idempotent replay, integrity conflict, or a rejection,” with only failed bearer authentication explicitly excluded; neither “classifies” nor the set of recorded rejections is defined
open_points.question: Which failures occur inside the import-result boundary and receive a fresh `import_id`, and which failures are rejected by HTTP parsing, validation, authorization, Registry access, or infrastructure handling without an import result?
options: Every request with an authenticated bearer receives an import result, including malformed contract and infrastructure/Registry failures
Only syntactically valid authenticated snapshot commands receive import results
Only business outcomes receive import results; transport, schema, Registry and infrastructure failures do not
open_points.default_guess: Create an import result for every authenticated, syntactically parseable import command; leave transport/parser and infrastructure failures outside that record.

witness.initial: A producer has a valid bearer credential and project grant.
events: The producer submits JSON with an unsupported `contract_version`.
The producer examines the response and later requests an import result.
outcomes: The rejection has a fresh `import_id` and is retrievable under R0-21.
The request fails schema/contract validation before classification and no import result exists.

open_points.subject: rejected snapshot-import result contents
open_points.text: R0-25 says a rejection is stored and answered as an immutable “import result,” while Audit mentions rejection reasons, but the text does not state which rejection facts are exposed to the producer
open_points.question: What minimum fields and producer-visible reason information must a rejected import result contain, especially for explicit errors such as foreign currency, integrity conflict, inactive project, missing grant, unsupported contract, and Registry failure?
options: Stable outcome code plus safe reason code and relevant estimate/project identifiers
Only a generic rejected outcome; detailed reasons remain audit-only
Different result shapes for validation, authorization, lifecycle and dependency failures
open_points.default_guess: Expose a closed safe reason code, `import_id`, submitted identity when safely parsed, and no sensitive project data; retain technical detail only in audit.

witness.initial: A valid producer submits a EUR snapshot for an archived project.
events: The portal records a fresh rejected import result.
The producer reads that result by `import_id`.
outcomes: The result identifies the safe reason `project_archived`, allowing the producer to stop retrying.
The result says only `rejected`, so the producer cannot distinguish a permanent lifecycle rejection from a transient failure.

open_points.subject: meaning of archived producer grants retaining access
open_points.text: Invariant 5 says an archived project's “existing grants and assignments keep giving access,” but a ServicePrincipal has only import and own-import-result capabilities, archived projects refuse imports, and R0-21 reads import results without rechecking the producer grant
open_points.question: What access, if any, does an existing producer grant continue to confer after archival, or should the retained-access statement be limited to viewer grants and staff assignments?
options: Producer grants remain stored but confer no usable archived-project operation
Producer grants confer some explicitly named archived-project read
The phrase “keep giving access” applies only to viewer grants and staff assignments
open_points.default_guess: Clarify that producer grants remain recorded and revocable but confer no usable archived-project operation; own import-result reads remain independent under R0-21.

witness.initial: A producer has a grant for project P and has previously imported a snapshot; Registry then archives P.
events: The producer attempts a project-scoped read using the retained grant.
The producer reads its earlier import result by `import_id`.
outcomes: No project-scoped read exists; only the grant-independent import-result read succeeds.
The retained producer grant is interpreted as authorizing an archived snapshot or budget read.
